{"id": "1b2e552f-bc3b-47aa-820d-4fb9d1c8d50c", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Given only those facts, here's what can and can't be reported:

**What can be reported:**
- The **list of AWS and third-party tool calls** this specific investigation made — that's what the journal actually contains (which services/tools were invoked, and presumably what they were used for).

**What cannot be reported:**
- Any **per-investigation billed cost or agent-seconds figure**. The 600-second metric is a Space-and-day aggregate covering multiple investigations and chats with no per-investigation breakdown, and the journal itself doesn't log execution-level billed seconds. There's no allocation key (no per-investigation seconds, no proportional weighting basis like tool-call count tied to actual billed time) that lets you split the 600 seconds back out to this one investigation without guessing.

**Why I won't estimate a number:** Dividing 600 seconds evenly across "several investigations and chats," or weighting by this investigation's tool-call count, would produce a figure that looks precise but is fabricated — it's not derivable from the supplied facts. I'd rather say clearly what's missing than hand you a plausible-looking cost that doesn't hold up.

If you want an actual per-investigation cost, that would require either execution-level billed-seconds data in the journal (not present here) or a defined attribution method from AWS/AIDevOps for splitting the aggregate metric — neither of which is part of what you've given me to work with.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
